events.title: Diocletian and Maximian abdicate together
events.description: In ceremonies at Nicomedia and Milan, the two senior emperors stepped down in favour of Galerius and Constantius. The planned handover soon broke down into civil war among their successors.
events.html: In ceremonies at Nicomedia and Milan, the two senior emperors stepped down in favour of Galerius and Constantius. The planned handover soon broke down into civil war among their successors.

events.title: A council at Carthage condemns the teachings of Pelagius
events.description: Bishops met under Aurelius of Carthage to act against the errors of Caelestius, a disciple of Pelagius, and denounced Pelagian doctrines of human nature, original sin, grace and perfectibility. The council fully approved the contrary views of Augustine.
events.html: Bishops met under Aurelius of Carthage to act against the errors of Caelestius, a disciple of Pelagius, and denounced Pelagian doctrines of human nature, original sin, grace and perfectibility. The council fully approved the contrary views of Augustine.

events.title: England ratifies the Treaty of Edinburgh-Northampton
events.description: Meeting at Northampton, the English Parliament ratified the treaty recognising Robert the Bruce as king of an independent Scotland. It ended the First War of Scottish Independence, though peace did not last.
events.html: Meeting at Northampton, the English Parliament ratified the treaty recognising Robert the Bruce as king of an independent Scotland. It ended the First War of Scottish Independence, though peace did not last.

events.title: James II's forces defeat the Black Douglases at Arkinholm
events.description: At Arkinholm near Langholm, a small action of only a few hundred troops decided the civil war between King James II and the Black Douglases, the most powerful noble family in Scotland. The win was a step towards a strong centralised Scottish monarchy.
events.html: At Arkinholm near Langholm, a small action of only a few hundred troops decided the civil war between King James II and the Black Douglases, the most powerful noble family in Scotland. The win was a step towards a strong centralised Scottish monarchy.

events.title: Acts of Union create the Kingdom of Great Britain
events.description: The union of England and Scotland took effect, creating a single kingdom and a single Parliament at Westminster. Scotland kept its own legal system and established church.
events.html: The union of England and Scotland took effect, creating a single kingdom and a single Parliament at Westminster. Scotland kept its own legal system and established church.

events.title: Adam Weishaupt founds the Bavarian Illuminati
events.description: Law professor Adam Weishaupt founded a secret society to spread Enlightenment ideas in Catholic Bavaria. It was banned in the 1780s but has lived on in conspiracy theories ever since.
events.html: Law professor Adam Weishaupt founded a secret society to spread Enlightenment ideas in Catholic Bavaria. It was banned in the 1780s but has lived on in conspiracy theories ever since.

events.title: Britain issues the Penny Black, the first adhesive stamp
events.description: The Penny Black went on sale, valid for postage from 6 May. Prepaid at a flat rate under Rowland Hill's reforms, it made letters affordable for ordinary people.
events.html: The Penny Black went on sale, valid for postage from 6 May. Prepaid at a flat rate under Rowland Hill's reforms, it made letters affordable for ordinary people.

events.title: American workers strike for an eight-hour day
events.description: Hundreds of thousands of workers across the United States walked out to demand an eight-hour day. Events in Chicago that week, culminating at Haymarket, led to 1 May becoming International Workers' Day.
events.html: Hundreds of thousands of workers across the United States walked out to demand an eight-hour day. Events in Chicago that week, culminating at Haymarket, led to 1 May becoming International Workers' Day.

events.title: Empire State Building opens in New York
events.description: President Hoover pressed a button in Washington to switch on the lights of the newly finished skyscraper. At 381 metres it remained the world's tallest building for nearly forty years.
events.html: President Hoover pressed a button in Washington to switch on the lights of the newly finished skyscraper. At 381 metres it remained the world's tallest building for nearly forty years.

events.title: Soviet missile downs a US U-2 spy plane
events.description: A U-2 piloted by Francis Gary Powers was shot down near Sverdlovsk. Washington's initial cover story collapsed when Moscow produced the pilot, wrecking the Paris summit two weeks later.
events.html: A U-2 piloted by Francis Gary Powers was shot down near Sverdlovsk. Washington's initial cover story collapsed when Moscow produced the pilot, wrecking the Paris summit two weeks later.

events.title: George W. Bush declares major combat in Iraq over
events.description: Speaking aboard USS Abraham Lincoln beneath a 'Mission Accomplished' banner, the president announced the end of major combat operations. The insurgency that followed made the moment notorious.
events.html: Speaking aboard USS Abraham Lincoln beneath a 'Mission Accomplished' banner, the president announced the end of major combat operations. The insurgency that followed made the moment notorious.

events.title: US special forces kill Osama bin Laden in Pakistan
events.description: Navy SEALs raided a compound in Abbottabad and killed the al-Qaeda leader behind the 11 September attacks. President Obama announced it that night, US time; in Pakistan it was early on 2 May.
events.html: Navy SEALs raided a compound in Abbottabad and killed the al-Qaeda leader behind the 11 September attacks. President Obama announced it that night, US time; in Pakistan it was early on 2 May.

intl.name: International Workers' Day
intl.description: Observed in over 160 countries, International Workers' Day commemorates the 1886 Haymarket affair in Chicago and celebrates the global labour movement's historic struggles for fair wages, safe conditions, and workers' rights.

song: A Japanese school song of 1914 about someone far from home who misses the hills and fields where they grew up.
